header.userPrompt:
Implement the FULL fix for GitHub issue #179 (read it first: `gh issue view 179`; its body was corrected: plain logout must NOT invalidate other sessions). The PR may say "Closes #179". Two parts: (A) reset-token fixes, (B) session invalidation.

Part A (reset token), small:
- ResetPasswordAction.scala (~31-39) and UsersRepository.scala (~108-115): delete the token inside the resetPassword transaction (compare `verify` ~93-106 which already deletes).
- UserTokensDAO.scala (~29-36) / ValidateUserToken.scala: the lookup must filter by token_type so an email verification token is not accepted by the reset endpoint (and vice versa).
- On password reset and on password change, delete all of the user's outstanding tokens.
- Tests: reset token cannot be used twice; a verification token is rejected by reset; other outstanding tokens are gone after reset.

Part B (sessions). Problem: login sets a signed Play cookie with only `id` (`server/src/main/scala/controllers/package.scala`, setSession ~line 22, authHandler ~line 51-66). authHandler never checks the DB, the cookie has no expiry, and logout, password change and password reset do not invalidate other sessions. A copied cookie stays valid forever.

Design (decided, follow it):
1. New evolution (use the next contiguous number, check existing files; Play needs contiguous numbers, no `;` inside comments): `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN session_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. No CHECK constraints.
2. Login puts the user's current `session_version` in the cookie next to `id`.
3. authHandler loads the user's current session_version (user-scoped, indexed PK lookup) and returns Unauthorized when the cookie's version is missing or different. Cookies issued before this change have no version and are rejected (users log in once after deploy). authHandler is currently a package-level implicit with no injected dependencies and controllers must not call repositories (layering is compiler-enforced): move the check behind a small action (e.g. ValidateSessionAction) reached through an injected class, keep the layering wart green with no new suppressions.
4. Bump session_version (`UPDATE users SET session_version = session_version + 1 WHERE user_id = ?`) in the same transaction as: password change, password reset, and a new explicit "log out everywhere" action. After a bump, re-issue the cookie for the request that triggered it where appropriate (password change by the logged-in user must not log that user out of the current device unexpectedly; decide cleanly and document in a code comment on intent).
5. Plain logout keeps clearing only the current cookie. It must NOT bump the version, other devices stay signed in.
6. Set a session `maxAge` (30 days) via Play session config so a stolen cookie eventually expires.
7. "Log out everywhere": Tapir endpoint in lib/api/shared, controller, action, ApiClient method, and a button reachable from an existing account/profile page in web (CLAUDE.md frontend reachability rule), with a confirm and form/Enter-key conventions from the repo.

Out of scope: auth throttling and captcha (#181), a per-device sessions table.

Acceptance (regression tests that fail before and pass after; follow docs/guide/testing.md, only targeted specs plus the full suite once at the end as the flow does):
- A cookie from before a password reset is rejected after the reset; same after password change and after "log out everywhere".
- Plain logout does not invalidate a second session of the same user.
- A cookie without a version is rejected; a cookie with the current version is accepted.
- The existing auth/controller specs still pass.
Placeholder data only (public repo), no external calls in tests, scalafmtAll + scalafmtSbt, follow CLAUDE.md. No Claude session links in commit messages or the PR.

resultJson.description:
Fix GitHub issue #179 (the PR may say "Closes #179"). Password recovery does not reliably lock out a third party. Part A: a reset-password token can be used more than once, and its type is never checked. The lookup in `UserTokensDAO.find(userId, token)` ignores `token_type`, so an email-verification token is accepted by `/users/reset-password` and the other way round. Outstanding tokens also survive a password reset or change. After this work, every token lookup filters by the expected `UserTokenType`. A password reset or password change deletes all of the user's outstanding tokens, including the one just used, inside the same repository transaction as the password write.

Part B: today the session is a signed Play cookie that holds only `id`. `authHandler` never checks the DB, the cookie never expires, and a copied cookie stays valid forever. This work adds `users.session_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (evolution 21). Login writes the current version into the cookie next to `id`. Every authenticated request compares the cookie's version with the DB value through a new `ValidateSessionAction`, reached from an injected `controllers` class, so the package-level implicit goes away and the layering wart stays green with no new suppressions. A missing or different version gives the existing "Unauthorized: Invalid or missing authentication" error, so cookies issued before deploy are rejected once. The version is bumped in the same transaction as a password change, a password reset, and a new explicit "log out everywhere" action. A password change re-issues the cookie for the device that made the request, so that device stays signed in. Log out everywhere clears the current cookie as well. Plain logout still only clears the current cookie and does NOT bump the version, so other devices stay signed in. The session also gets `maxAge = 30 days`, enforced by Play's JWT `exp`.

Out of scope: auth throttling and captcha (#181), a per-device sessions table, cookie `secure`, and the email-body logging point in the issue. Tests are regression tests that fail before the change and pass after. They use placeholder data only and make no external calls. Run targeted specs only (`sbt "testOnly *XSpec"`, `CI=true sbt Test/compile`). The full suite runs once at the end of the flow. Format with `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`. No Claude session links in commits or the PR.

tasks.title: Reset/verification tokens: filter by type, single use, purge on password reset/change
tasks.description:
Part A, backend only.
- `UserTokensDAO.find(userId, token)` → add `tokenType: UserTokenType` and `AND token_type = ${tokenType.entryName}::TEXT`. Mirror the change in `UserTokensRepository.find(userId, token, tokenType)`. Callers: `ResetPasswordAction` passes `UserTokenType.ResetPassword`, `VerifyUserEmailAction` passes `UserTokenType.EmailVerification`. Update existing callers and specs (`UserTokensRepositorySpec` 'find(userId, token)').
- Add `UserTokensDAO.deleteAll(userId: UUID)` (`DELETE FROM user_tokens WHERE user_id = ?`).
- `UsersRepository.resetPassword` and `UsersRepository.updatePassword`: call `UserTokensDAO.deleteAll(userId)` inside the existing `withTransaction`. This also deletes the reset token that was just used. Leave `verify` as is.
- Tests:
  - UsersControllerSpec 'POST /reset-password': the same reset token used twice → the second call fails with the not-found message (`Token for user <id> wasn't found`).
  - A verification token, from `createUser` with a mocked `tokenGenerator` and no verify step, is rejected by `resetPassword`.
  - After a reset, `userTokensRepository.find(userId)` is empty, even when another token was outstanding, e.g. a second forgot-password token.
  - The reverse case: a reset token is rejected by `verifyEmail` for an unverified user (a forgot-password call needs a verified user, so build it at repository level or assert on the DAO/repository type filter in UserTokensRepositorySpec).
  - UsersRepositorySpec: `updatePassword` and `resetPassword` remove all tokens of that user only (another user's token survives).
- Verify: `sbt "testOnly *UsersControllerSpec *UsersRepositorySpec *UserTokensRepositorySpec *AuthControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Add users.session_version (evolution 21) and bump it in password reset/change
tasks.description:
Persistence groundwork for sessions. It has no effect on auth yet.
- New `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/21.sql`: `-- !Ups`, a short comment with NO `;` inside comments, then `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN session_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;`. No CHECK constraint, no Downs, matching the style of 20.sql.
- `repositories/models/User.scala`: add `sessionVersion: Int`. Add `"session_version"` to `userParser` in `repositories/daos/package.scala`, and add `session_version` to every `SELECT` in `UsersDAO` (all, find(email), find(userId), findUserForUpdate). Fix any `User(...)` construction that breaks (CreateUserAction ~line 51 maps to a response; check it compiles). Chimney `transformInto[Login.Response]` ignores the extra field.
- `UsersDAO`: `findSessionVersion(userId): Option[Int]` (PK lookup) and `bumpSessionVersion(userId): Int` (`UPDATE users SET session_version = session_version + 1 WHERE user_id = ? RETURNING session_version`). Use `.as(SqlParser.int("session_version").single)`.
- `UsersRepository`:
  - `findSessionVersion(userId): Future[Option[Int]]` using `withConnection`.
  - `resetPassword(...)` bumps inside its transaction and still returns `Future[Unit]`.
  - `updatePassword(...)` bumps inside its transaction and returns `Future[Int]`, the new version, because the next task re-issues the cookie from it. Adjust `UpdatePasswordAction` to compile (still returns Unit for now).
  - New `logoutEverywhere(userId): Future[Int]`: transaction with the bump plus a `UserLogsDAO` entry such as "Logged out of all sessions".
- Tests in UsersRepositorySpec:
  - A new user has version 0.
  - resetPassword, updatePassword and logoutEverywhere each increment by exactly 1, and updatePassword/logoutEverywhere return the new value.
  - Another user's version is untouched.
  - `findSessionVersion` of an unknown id is None.
- Remember the MEMORY note: a `;` inside a `--` comment breaks every DB spec.
- Verify: `sbt "testOnly *UsersRepositorySpec *UsersControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Move authHandler into an injected SessionAuthenticator (behaviour-neutral refactor)
tasks.description:
Prepares DI for the DB check without changing behaviour.
- New `server/src/main/scala/controllers/SessionAuthenticator.scala`:
  - `class SessionAuthenticator @Inject() ()(implicit ec: ExecutionContext)`, with an `implicit val authHandler: ServerRequest => Future[UUID]` (or a `given`). For now its body is today's logic moved from `controllers/package.scala`: read the Play session from `serverRequest.underlying.asInstanceOf[RequestHeader]`, parse `id`, and recover any failure to `RuntimeException("Unauthorized: Invalid or missing authentication")`.
  - Keep the single existing `@SuppressWarnings(Array("org.wartremover.warts.AsInstanceOf"))` with its justification. It moves with the code; do not add a new suppression.
- Delete the package-level `implicit def authHandler` from `controllers/package.scala`.
- Every controller whose routes use `userAuth` endpoints must inject `sessionAuthenticator: SessionAuthenticator` and `import sessionAuthenticator.authHandler` (or `.given`) so the endpoint defs resolve the implicit. The list: Auth, Users, Categories, Merchants, ImportRules, Expenses, Receipts, BankStatements, BankStatementTemplates, Refunds, Savings, Subscriptions, Documents. Grep for `Future[UUID]` / `userIdF` under `server/src/main/scala/controllers` to confirm.
- `net.wiringbits.routing.ApiRouter`: the companion `object ApiRouter.routes` currently resolves the package implicit to build Swagger endpoint docs. Inject `SessionAuthenticator` into the class and build the Swagger endpoint list there with its handler (routing → controllers is an allowed edge), or pass the handler explicitly. Do not keep a dummy handler that would be used to serve requests.
- Update docs/guide/backend.md RULE-BE-002 (and its `@file` pointer) to point at `SessionAuthenticator`.
- No behaviour change, so the existing specs are the test.
- Verify: `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (the layering wart must stay green), then `sbt "testOnly *AuthControllerSpec *UsersControllerSpec *CategoriesControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Enforce session_version: versioned cookie, ValidateSessionAction, cookie re-issue on password change, 30-day maxAge
tasks.description:
The core of part B.
- Shared server model `net.wiringbits.models.UserSession(userId: UUID, version: Int)`. It lives in the shared leaf, reachable from controllers and actions, and is NOT the web contract.
- `PlayTapirBridge.setSession(session: UserSession)` writes `Map("id" -> ..., "sessionVersion" -> version.toString)`.
- `LoginAction` returns `(Login.Response, UserSession)`, with the version from the `User` row it already loads (`user.sessionVersion`). AuthController.login passes it to setSession, and the JSON response is unchanged.
- New `net.wiringbits.actions.auth.ValidateSessionAction @Inject()(usersRepository: UsersRepository)`: `apply(session: UserSession): Future[UUID]`. It loads `usersRepository.findSessionVersion(userId)` and passes the comparison to a new validator `net.wiringbits.validations.ValidateSessionVersion(current: Option[Int], presented: Int)`. The validator throws when the user is missing or the version differs (RULE-BE-009: no inline `if` in actions).
- `SessionAuthenticator` injects `ValidateSessionAction`. It parses `id` + `sessionVersion` from the cookie (missing or unparsable version → fail), then calls the action. Every failure is recovered to the exact message `Unauthorized: Invalid or missing authentication`.
- Password change keeps the current device signed in:
  - `UsersEndpoints.updatePassword` adds `.out(setSessionHeader)`, so the output becomes `(UpdatePassword.Response, String)`.
  - `UpdatePasswordAction` returns the new `UserSession` from `usersRepository.updatePassword`'s `Int`.
  - `UsersController.updatePassword` re-issues the cookie through `playTapirBridge.setSession`. Add a code comment on intent: the bump revokes every other device, and re-issuing the cookie keeps the device that changed the password signed in.
  - Password reset does not re-issue: the endpoint is unauthenticated.
  - Plain logout is unchanged (clears the cookie, no bump). Add a short comment saying so on purpose.
- `ApiClient.updatePassword`: rewrite it like `login`. Send the saved cookies, use `.response(asStringAlways)`, and replace `lastAuthResponse` only on a successful (non-ErrorResponse) body, so the JVM test client keeps working. The web caller signature `Future[UpdatePassword.Response]` must not change. The browser updates its cookie from Set-Cookie on its own.
- `application.conf` `play.http.session`: `maxAge = 30 days`, with a comment that Play's JWT `expiresAfter` defaults to it, so expiry is enforced server-side too.
- Tests:
  - ValidateSessionAction spec (PostgresSpec/RepositorySpec style, data via RepositoryUtils): current version accepted; stale version rejected; unknown user rejected.
  - AuthControllerSpec:
    - A cookie without a version is rejected. Build it with `app.injector.instanceOf[play.api.mvc.SessionCookieBaker].encodeAsCookie(Session(Map("id" -> userId.toString)))` + `CookieHeaderEncoding.encodeCookieHeader`, and send a raw sttp `GET http://localhost:$port/auth/me` with that Cookie header. Expect the Unauthorized body.
    - A cookie with the current version is accepted.
    - Plain logout on client A leaves client B (same user, separate `withApiClient`, both logged in) able to call `currentUser`.
    - The login Set-Cookie carries a Max-Age (or assert the config value).
  - UsersControllerSpec:
    - Client A logs in, then the password is reset by token → A.currentUser fails with Unauthorized.
    - Clients A and B log in; A changes the password → B is rejected and A still works.
- Verify: `sbt "testOnly *AuthControllerSpec *UsersControllerSpec *ValidateSessionActionSpec"`, plus one other controller spec, e.g. `*CategoriesControllerSpec`, to confirm logged-in flows still pass.

tasks.title: "Log out everywhere" backend: endpoint, action, controller, ApiClient
tasks.description:
- Contract `lib/api/shared/.../api/models/auth/LogoutEverywhere.scala`: `Request()`/`Response()` with play-json `Format`s, mirroring `Logout`.
- `AuthEndpoints.logoutEverywhere(implicit authHandler)`: `POST /auth/logout-everywhere`, `.in(userAuth)`, `.out(jsonBody[LogoutEverywhere.Response])`, `.out(setSessionHeader)`, `.errorOut(oneOf(HttpErrors.badRequest))`, plus a summary and description stating that it signs out every session, including this one. Add it to `AuthEndpoints.routes`.
- `net.wiringbits.actions.auth.LogoutEverywhereAction @Inject()(usersRepository)`: `apply(userId): Future[Unit]` calls `usersRepository.logoutEverywhere(userId)` (a bump + user log in one transaction, from an earlier task).
- `AuthController.logoutEverywhere(userIdF)`: `handleRequest`, `logger.info(s"Logout everywhere: $userId")`, the action, then `playTapirBridge.clearSession()` to clear the current device too. Wire it in `routes`.
- `ApiClient.logoutEverywhere: Future[LogoutEverywhere.Response]`: built like `logout`. Send the saved cookies, and call `unsafeRemoveLoginResponse()` only on success.
- Tests:
  - LogoutEverywhereAction spec: the version increments and the user log is written; another user is unaffected.
  - AuthControllerSpec: clients A and B log in, A calls logoutEverywhere → both A and B get Unauthorized on `currentUser`; unauthenticated call → Unauthorized.
- Verify: `sbt "testOnly *AuthControllerSpec *LogoutEverywhereActionSpec"`.

tasks.title: Web: "Log out of all devices" button with confirm dialog on the user page
tasks.description:
- In `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/UserEditPage.scala` (route `/me`, already reachable from the app bar user menu), add a new section after `mcpSection`, using the same Container/Card/Box column layout. It has a heading ("Sessions"), a short explanation, and an outlined/error-colour `mui.Button` "Log out of all devices".
- Clicking the button opens an MUI `Dialog` confirm, following the existing pattern in `components/pages/expenses/ExpensesPage.scala` (~1135-1160) or `BankStatementsPage.scala` (~263-300): `DialogTitle`, `DialogContentText`, then `DialogActions` with Cancel and Confirm. Put the confirm action inside `form(onSubmit := ...)` with the confirm button `type("submit")` so Enter confirms (RULE-FE-008).
- On confirm: disable the buttons while working, call `props.ctx.api.client.logoutEverywhere.onComplete`. On Success, call `props.ctx.loggedOut()` and navigate to `/` (as `AppRouter.signOut` does, or use `useHistory`). On Failure, show `ErrorLabel(ex.getMessage)`. Guard state updates with the existing `mounted` ref.
- Follow frontend.md: no object-level `val` React elements, `def` for elements reused in the tree, `Hooks.useState` for dialog-open/working/error state, no setTimeout hacks.
- Tests: no DOM test unless it guards a known runtime failure (RULE-TE-010). If any pure helper is extracted, unit-test it.
- Verify: `CI=true sbt web/compile`. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (see memory). Optionally run `sbt "web/testOnly *UserEditPage*"` if a spec exists.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/: Tapir endpoints (endpoints/*.scala), contract models (models/**), and ApiClient.scala, which both the JVM tests and the Scala.js web app use. endpoints/package.scala defines `setSessionHeader` (the Set-Cookie header out), `errorResponseErrorOut`, and `def userAuth(implicit handleAuth: ServerRequest => Future[UUID]) = extractFromRequest(handleAuth)`. Every protected endpoint is a `def x(implicit authHandler: ServerRequest => Future[UUID])`, and `routes(implicit authHandler)` lists them.
- server/: Play 3 + Pekko + Tapir + Anorm + Postgres, Scala 3. Layers are compiler-enforced by the Layering wart, configured in server/.wartremover-layering.conf. The relevant edges: controllers → {mcp, actions, apis, shared}; actions → {services, validations, repositories, apis, dbmodels, shared}; validations → {repositories, apis, dbmodels, shared}; repositories → {daos, dbmodels, shared}; routing → {controllers, shared}. dbmodels = net.wiringbits.repositories.models, so controllers can NOT touch `User`/`UserToken` rows. shared = net.wiringbits.{models, config, executors, util, api, common}. Actions don't call actions. Repositories own transactions: `Future { database.withTransaction { implicit conn => DAO calls } }`, never composed futures (RULE-BE-005/006). DAOs are synchronous Anorm `SQL"""..."""`. Validators throw RuntimeException; conditionals belong in validations/, not inline in actions (RULE-BE-009). Controllers: `handleRequest { for {...} yield Right(...) }` plus `logger.info` with non-sensitive ids only.
- web/: Scala.js + Slinky + MUI5. Pages live in web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages, and the API is reached as `props.ctx.api.client`.

KEY FILES
- server/src/main/scala/controllers/package.scala: `class PlayTapirBridge @Inject()(requestFactory: DefaultRequestFactory, cookieHeaderEncoding: CookieHeaderEncoding)` with `setSession(userId: UUID): Future[String]` (it builds `Session(Map("id"->...))`, then `requestFactory.sessionBaker.encodeAsCookie`, then `encodeSetCookieHeader`) and `clearSession()`. It also holds `handleRequest`, `errorHandler`, and today's `implicit def authHandler(serverRequest: ServerRequest)(implicit ec): Future[UUID]`. That handler casts `serverRequest.underlying.asInstanceOf[RequestHeader].session` under `@SuppressWarnings(Array("org.wartremover.warts.AsInstanceOf"))`, reads "id", and recovers to `RuntimeException("Unauthorized: Invalid or missing authentication")`. Tests assert that exact message.
- Controllers resolve the implicit authHandler only because they share `package controllers`. The ones with userAuth endpoints: Auth, Users, Categories, Merchants, ImportRules, Expenses, Receipts, BankStatements, BankStatementTemplates, Refunds, Savings, Subscriptions, Documents. McpController, TelegramWebApp, TelegramBot, Health and EnvironmentConfig don't use it. No test constructs controllers by hand; all go through Guice.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/routing/ApiRouter.scala: the class injects the controllers. `object ApiRouter.routes(implicit ec)` builds the Swagger endpoint list and gets authHandler from `import controllers.*`.
- controllers/AuthController.scala: login (`loginAction(body)`, then `playTapirBridge.setSession(response.id)`), me, logout (clears the cookie only).
- controllers/UsersController.scala: resetPassword (`resetPasswordAction(userId, token, password)`), updatePassword (`updatePasswordAction(userId, request)`).
- actions/auth/LoginAction.scala: returns `user.transformInto[Login.Response]` (id, name, email).
- actions/users/ResetPasswordAction.scala: HMACs the token with `TokensHelper.doHMACSHA1(token.toString.getBytes, userTokensConfig.hmacSecret)`, then `userTokensRepository.find(userId, hmac)`, then `ValidateUserToken(token)` (expiry only), then `usersRepository.resetPassword(userId, hashed, EmailMessage.resetPassword(name))`.
- actions/users/VerifyUserEmailAction.scala: the same token lookup, then `usersRepository.verify(userId, tokenId, msg)`, which deletes that token.
- actions/users/UpdatePasswordAction.scala: `ValidatePasswordMatches(maybeUser, old, hasher)`, then `usersRepository.updatePassword(userId, hashed, EmailMessage.updatePassword(name))`.
- repositories/UsersRepository.scala: create/find/update/updatePassword/verify/resetPassword. Its private `sendEmailLater(userId, msg)(implicit conn)` enqueues a BackgroundJob inside the transaction.
- repositories/UserTokensRepository.scala and daos/UserTokensDAO.scala: create, find(userId, token), find(userId), delete(tokenId, userId). Table user_tokens(user_token_id, token, token_type TEXT, created_at, expires_at, user_id).
- repositories/models/UserTokenType.scala: `enum UserTokenType extends DbEnum { EmailVerification, ResetPassword }`. `entryName` is stored in the column.
- daos/UsersDAO.scala: explicit column lists in each SELECT (user_id, name, email, password, created_at, verified_on). `userParser` in daos/package.scala is `Macro.parser[User](...)` with named columns. `resetPassword(userId, pw)` updates the password.
- repositories/models/User.scala: `case class User(id, name, email, hashedPassword, createdAt, verifiedOn)`.
- services/EmailsHelper.scala: creates the verification/reset tokens.
- Evolutions live in server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/1..20.sql, so the next one is 21.sql. Style: `-- !Ups`, a comment, the SQL; no Downs in any file. NEVER put `;` inside a `--` comment: Play splits on it and every DB spec fails. users PK is `users_user_id_pk (user_id)`.
- server/src/main/resources/application.conf: block `play.http.session { cookieName, secure, domain, path }`. Add `maxAge = 30 days` here. Play's JWT session `expiresAfter` defaults to `${play.http.session.maxAge}`.
- ApiClient.scala: `handleRequest` sends `lastAuthResponse.map(_.unsafeCookies)` as cookies and never stores response cookies. `login` stores the whole response through `unsafeSetLoginResponse`, and `logout` clears it through `unsafeRemoveLoginResponse`. Protected calls pass `dummyUserId` for the `Future[UUID]` input, via `private implicit val handleDummyUserId`. Any endpoint that re-issues or clears the cookie must update `lastAuthResponse` the way login/logout do, and only on success, or the JVM test client breaks.
- web: pages/UserEditPage.scala is route `/me`, reached from the user menu. It has Tabs (summary/password via widgets/EditPasswordForm.scala, which calls `ctx.api.client.updatePassword(request).onComplete`) plus Telegram and MCP Card sections. Use it as the layout template, and use its `mounted` ref to guard state updates. AppRouter.scala `signOut` route: `ctx.api.client.logout.onComplete { Success => props.ctx.loggedOut() }; Redirect("/")`. For confirm dialogs, see ExpensesPage.scala ~1135-1220 and BankStatementsPage.scala ~263-300 (`mui.Dialog`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogContent(DialogContentText(...))`, `DialogActions`). Forms: `form(onSubmit := (handleSubmit(_)))` with a submit-type button so Enter works (frontend.md RULE-FE-008).

TESTING
- docs/guide/testing.md: `should` subjects never repeat the class name. Use `.futureValue`, and `.expectError` (from PlayPostgresSpec) to get a failed future's message.
- Repository and action specs extend `RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils` and use `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`. Seed data through RepositoryUtils (`createUser()`, `createToken(userId)`), never raw SQL. Values must be random and assertions user-scoped, because the Postgres container is shared.
- Controller specs (e.g. server/src/test/scala/controllers/UsersControllerSpec.scala, AuthControllerSpec.scala) extend `PlayPostgresSpec with LoginUtils with MockitoSugar`. They override `guiceApplicationBuilder(container)` with mocks for EmailApi, ReCaptchaApi, Clock and TokenGenerator.
  - `withApiClient { implicit client => ... }` makes a fresh client, i.e. its own cookie jar. Nest two of them to simulate two devices.
  - `createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator, emailMaybe=...)` mocks `tokenGenerator.next()` for the verification token, then creates, verifies and logs in. The default password is "test123...".
  - For forgot/reset: `when(tokenGenerator.next()).thenReturn(uuid)`, then `client.forgotPassword(ForgotPassword.Request(email, Captcha.trusted("test")))`, then `client.resetPassword(ResetPassword.Request(UserToken(userId, uuid), Password.trusted("test456...")))`.
  - The not-found error for a token is `s"Token for user $userId wasn't found"`.
  - To hand-craft a cookie: `app.injector.instanceOf[play.api.mvc.SessionCookieBaker].encodeAsCookie(Session(Map(...)))` plus `app.injector.instanceOf[CookieHeaderEncoding].encodeCookieHeader(Seq(cookie))`, sent with sttp `basicRequest` and `HttpClientFutureBackend()` to `http://localhost:$port/auth/me`.
- RULE-TE-011: new actions get a PostgresSpec behaviour test; controller tests stay thin, covering auth plus encoding. Older controllers are grandfathered for end-to-end behaviour tests.
- Build:
  - Typecheck with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (this is `-Werror`, and the Layering wart runs at compile).
  - Run targeted specs with `sbt "testOnly *XSpec"`. Don't run the full `sbt test` during tasks.
  - Before finishing: `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`.
  - Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default node is v16).
  - BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec is known to be flaky.

NON-OBVIOUS
- Changing an endpoint's output to add `setSessionHeader` changes its Tapir type to `(X.Response, String)`. The controller must then return the header string, and the ApiClient method must decode it. Keep the web-facing ApiClient signature `Future[X.Response]`.
- The Swagger list in `object ApiRouter` needs some authHandler once the package implicit is gone. Supply it from the injected `SessionAuthenticator` in the class (routing → controllers is allowed) instead of inventing a dummy that could serve requests.
- Keep the Unauthorized message string identical. Many specs assert it.
- Cookie key for the version: "sessionVersion". Cookies without it, i.e. everything issued before deploy, must be rejected.
- The `UsersRepository.updatePassword` return type changes to `Future[Int]`, the new version, so the controller can re-issue the cookie. `resetPassword` bumps too but needs no return value, because the reset endpoint is unauthenticated.
